name: ludifex
author: Cresmar Mat-an
description: ludifex is a 2D and 3D world library for C++20: physics over Box2D v3 and Box3D, a physically based renderer with optional compute-shader ray and path tracing, animation, and sound.
lead: Simulate worlds with Box2D and Box3D and render them with physically based shading, cascaded shadows, and optional ray and path tracing in compute shaders. Worlds can also step without a window, in a test or on a server.
example_title: A crate falling in a world
example_text: Worlds step without a window or a device: add a ground and a box, step three seconds, and read where the box came to rest.

features.title: Worlds and actors
features.text: 2D and 3D worlds, handle-based actors, fixed-step simulation with smooth interpolation, a transform hierarchy, and saving a world to bytes.

features.title: Physics
features.text: Collision events, sensors, collision layers, ray and shape casts, a character controller that handles steps and slopes, and joints with limits and motors.

features.title: Physically based rendering
features.text: Metallic-roughness shading, cascaded shadows, 256 clustered lights, a procedural sky, ambient occlusion, bloom, and quality presets from Potato to Extreme.

features.title: Ray and path tracing
features.text: Traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, and a progressive path tracer, all in compute shaders, so no ray-tracing hardware is needed.

features.title: Models and animation
features.text: glTF, FBX, OBJ, and the other formats Assimp reads, with skeletal animation, morph targets, and crossfading between clips.

features.title: Sound in the world
features.text: Positional sound on actors, distance falloff, Doppler shift, occlusion, a voice limit with priorities, and streamed music.

sibling.name: opane
sibling.text: opane gives a world its window, its interface, and its input. ludifex renders into it, full-window or inside a viewport in your layout, and the two share one device and one audio mix.
